newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - Sept 24.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - Sept 24.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

TeleTrak and Thoroughbred International Marketing will today announce details of a breeding venture at a press conference being convened by the Central Goldfields Shire Council, in a move sure to outrage the racing industry. Page 16.

According to Manly coach Bob Fulton, St George is obviously trying to deflect pressure from its players by playing down the effect of a rugby league grand final berth, but the size of the Dragons' supporter base will ultimately subject them to some pressure. Page 16.

The Hobart Devils may consider taking legal action against the National Basketball League after failing to prove they were financially viable to the league's board of directors in Melbourne on Saturday. Along with Geelong Supercats and Gold Coast Rollers Hobart will surrender its NBL licence at the end of the regular season. Page 16.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

In good news for coach John McKee, Eastwood's rugby union Test fullback Matt Burke is "a reasonable chance" of being available for the preliminary final against Randwick at Waratah Rugby Stadium on Saturday and Australian under-21 five-eighth Nathan Spooner is a certainty to play. Page 41.

Although he missed last night's light training run on the MCG, injured North Melbourne ruckman Corey McKernan said he would definitely play against Sydney in Saturday's AFL grand final, after jarring his knee against Brisbane on Saturday. Page 42.

Although referee David Manson admits he had cautioned Manly's Terry Hill for coming close to illegal blocking tactics during Sunday's 24-0 rugby league victory over Cronulla, he has described as a "red herring" the accusations by St George coach David Waite, in response to Waite's call for the referee to clamp down on the practice. Page 42.
THE AGE

Following his third-place finish in the Loch Lomond World Invitational yesterday, Australian golfer Robert Allenby has been cleared of having a broken foot after he tripped in a rut on his way to the car park soon after the final round. Page C6.

The AFL has pushed back the start of this year's grand final by 15 minutes to 2.45 p.m. to allow for more pre-match entertainment in the centenary celebrations which will be bigger than a normal grand final production. Page C8.

Airlines Ansett and Qantas have programmed additional flights and Countrylink has put on several coaches after its train services were fully booked, to cope with the demand for seats on the Sydney to Melbourne route from AFL fans going to the Melbourne grand final. Page C8.
HERALD SUN

The Sydney Swans club offices were faced with a barrage of complaints from angry fans yesterday after many missed out on AFL Grand Final tickets. There were only 7,500 tickets allocated by the AFL, for about 9,500 members who were eligible to buy finals tickets. Page 69.

Essendon's James Hird and Brisbane's Michael Voss last night finished on 21 votes each to win the AFL's Brownlow Medal. North Melbourne's Corey McKernan also polled 21 votes but was ineligible after being suspended for one week because of unduly rough play. Page 72.

The AFL yesterday ordered an investigation into the circumstances which forced a bloodied James Hird from the SCG during the first quarter of Saturday's preliminary final between Essendon and Sydney, in an inquiry which could see Swans defender Andrew Dunley before the AFL Tribunal this week. Page 72.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Back in Australia for the first time since coming second to Marie-Jose Perec in the 400m Olympic final, Atlanta silver medallist Cathy Freeman said yesterday that her second placing had increased her hunger to be world number one and she hoped to break the 48.63 seconds she ran in Atlanta. Page 62.

An auditor's report of rugby league club the South Queensland Crushers reveals the club has debts of almost A$9 million and could be closed as soon as Monday. The report also showed that players have only been paid for three of their 22 matches this seasn. Page 62.

Brisbane's Allan Langer has won rugby league's Dally M Player of the Year award, ahead of Canberra's Laurie Daley and Jim Dymock from Parramatta. Langer finished 18 points clear of the field, taking home an A$11,000 winner's cheque. Page 64.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
